lines.trans: Senya, maybe we started all this for nothing?
Just think what a great life awaits us!
You steal meat and immediately blame it on the poltergeist!
Question, who locked me in the shower room this morning?
Of course, the evil poltergeist did it!
And if you smell in the morning, is it stale alcohol breath?
You can easily blame that on the poltergeist too!
Well alright, look how scary it turned out!
It looks like real blood is painted on the mirror!
Fedya, that actually is real blood!
Relax, it is just ordinary pig's blood!
Alright, run quickly back to the kitchen!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'blood' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На зеркале будто настоящая кровь нарисована!
examples.trans: It looks like real blood is painted on the mirror!

examples.text: Федя, так это и есть настоящая кровь!
examples.trans: Fedya, that actually is real blood!

examples.text: Да расслабься ты, это обычная свиная кровь!
examples.trans: Relax, it is just ordinary pig's blood!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'рисованный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('drawn / painted').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень нарисованный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very drawn choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто нарисованный день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply drawn day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это вы его все так сильно ненавидели!
examples.trans: All of you hated him so much!

examples.text: А чего вы стоите такие смешные?
examples.trans: And why are you standing there looking so funny?

examples.text: Вы стоите так, будто привидение увидели!
examples.trans: You are standing there as if you saw a ghost!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

examples.text: Может быть, это настоящий полтергейст?
examples.trans: Could it be a real poltergeist?

examples.text: Давай, может быть, я тебе денег подброшу?
examples.trans: Come on, maybe I can toss some extra money your way?

examples.text: Я не согласен, всему должно быть логическое объяснение!
examples.trans: I disagree, there must be a logical explanation for everything!

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'relax!', paired with 'расслабляться'.

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься.
examples.trans: Vanya, relax.

examples.text: Я хочу расслабиться.
examples.trans: I want to relax.

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься. В этот раз без обмана.
examples.trans: Vanya, relax. This time there's no trick.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ordinary, usual').

examples.text: Да расслабься ты, это обычная свиная кровь!
examples.trans: Relax, it is just ordinary pig's blood!

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

examples.text: Это был обычный день.
examples.trans: It was an ordinary day.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'виной'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pig's / pork').

examples.text: Да расслабься ты, это обычная свиная кровь!
examples.trans: Relax, it is just ordinary pig's blood!

examples.text: Может, ты дома свинью по частям собираешь?
examples.trans: Maybe you are assembling a pig piece by piece at home?

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'run', paired with 'побежать'.

examples.text: Беги, Марина, пока не поздно!
examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!

examples.text: Куда ты так быстро бежишь?
examples.trans: Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.text: Всё, беги скорее обратно на кухню!
examples.trans: Alright, run quickly back to the kitchen!

examples.text: Скоро они все заикаться от страха будут, даже шеф!
examples.trans: Soon they will all be stuttering from fear, even the chef!

examples.text: Дима, такими темпами ты скоро без ресторана останешься!
examples.trans: Dima, at this rate you will soon be left without a restaurant!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Всё, беги скорее обратно на кухню!
examples.trans: Alright, run quickly back to the kitchen!

examples.text: Мне нужно там важные бумаги разобрать.
examples.trans: I need to sort through some important papers in there.

examples.text: Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Кухня — это настоящее высокое искусство.
examples.trans: Cuisine is a true high art.

examples.text: Подождите, что происходит со светом на кухне?
examples.trans: Wait, what is happening with the lights in the kitchen?

examples.text: Кухня — это искусство.
examples.trans: Cuisine is an art.
